items.title: New genome: Dictyostelium giganteum, now 20 hosted
items.body: The newly published Dictyostelium giganteum genome (Sharma et al. 2026, Genome Biology and Evolution) is now hosted here, bringing the site to 20 sequenced dictyostelid genomes. The assembly (NCBI GCA_059609475.1) and its annotation are in the genome browser, BLAST, the comparative species search, and the Downloads page, with gene models, restriction sites, and sequence downloads.

items.title: Download the sequences behind the genomes
items.body: You can now get the actual sequences three ways. In the genome browser, click any gene model to download its sequence as FASTA. On each D. discoideum gene's Orthologs tab, download that gene's orthologs as protein or CDS, one genome at a time or all at once in a single file. And on the Downloads page, every sequenced genome now has CDS (nucleotide) and protein (amino acid) FASTA files, one record per gene ID. With thanks to Tera Levin for the suggestions.

items.title: Curated protein and genetic interactions on gene pages
items.body: The Interactions tab now shows experimentally curated physical and genetic interactions from BioGRID, each with its experimental method and publication, alongside the predicted associations from STRING. It is a focused set for Dictyostelium today, and curators and authors can help grow it over time.

items.title: Two more dictyostelid genomes, 19 now hosted
items.body: D. citrinum KGL29A and D. intermedium PJ11, two genomes still working through GenBank's pipeline, are now hosted here directly. That brings the site to 19 sequenced dictyostelid genomes. Both are in the genome browser, BLAST, downloads, and the ortholog tables, using the sequencing team's own contig names and gene IDs. With thanks to Tera Levin and the Holland*, Ahmed* et al. 2025 team for sharing the assemblies.

items.title: Curated orthologs, and ortholog search in the browser
items.body: Two ortholog improvements. Each gene's Orthologs tab now shows curated ortholog calls across all the sequenced dictyostelid genomes, from the Holland*, Ahmed* et al. 2025 OrthoFinder groups, each linking straight to its locus in the genome browser, with paralogs flagged. And in the genome browser, typing a gene symbol while viewing another species jumps to that gene's ortholog there. The natural-variation panel now compares each strain against its true ortholog rather than the closest paralog.

items.title: Search by more than one phenotype, and download the results
items.body: Phenotype search can now combine several phenotypes at once. Enter multiple terms separated by a semicolon and choose all (AND) or any (OR), for example chemotaxis; aberrant fruiting body. Every result also has a one-click download of the matching gene list as a spreadsheet.

items.title: New downloads: the Stock Center catalog and BLAST results
items.body: The full Dicty Stock Center catalog, all strains and plasmids, is now downloadable as a spreadsheet from the Downloads page. On gene pages, the cross-species BLAST comparison now offers downloads of the hit table and a FASTA of the hit sequences.

items.title: GO annotations refreshed to the current release
items.body: The Gene Ontology annotations were refreshed to the current GO Consortium release: 68,097 annotations across 8,659 genes, up from 65,201. You can confirm the count on the Data and sources page.

items.title: See who studies each gene
items.body: Every gene record now shows the researchers who study that gene. Look for the new Researchers list on the Literature tab. It ranks the senior authors of the gene's papers by how many they have published, and each name links to that author's papers on the gene in PubMed. The list is built from the published literature, so it stays current on its own as new papers are indexed. You can also add your lab. If your group published on a gene where you were not the last author, use the "add your lab" link on the Literature tab to request a listing. A curator reviews each request before it appears.

items.title: Congratulations to the 2026 Dictyostelium award winners
items.body: Congratulations to the winners of the 2026 Dictyostelium awards! Lu Ma won the Graduate Student award. Xuehua Xu won the Research Scientist award. Fei Liu and Mélanie Foulon are co-winners of the Postdoctoral Researcher award. Jordi van Gestel and Elizabeth Ostrowski are co-winners of the Junior Faculty award. Congratulations to all the winners, and thank you to Dr. Richard Gomer for sponsoring these awards!

items.title: BLAST alignments, protein search, and the ListServ archive
items.body: Several updates are now live. BLAST results now show the full pairwise alignment for every hit. You can see exactly where your query matches, with the query and subject sequences lined up, instead of just a link to a genome location. The BLAST tool also gained a blastp option. It searches a protein query against every D. discoideum AX4 protein, and each hit links straight to its gene page. We also migrated the Dicty ListServ Archive from dictyBase. It holds the questions and answers sent to the dicty mailing list since 1997, organized by topic and fully searchable. Find it under Community. Finally, the literature search on each gene page is more precise. It now searches by the gene name alone, so results stay focused on the gene you are viewing.

items.title: More disease models, more phenotypes, and a downloads archive
items.body: Three data updates are now live. Phenotype search now covers about 1,200 genes, up from around 470. It was rebuilt from dictyBase's complete set of curated mutant phenotypes, so many more genes now turn up when you search by phenotype. The disease-model table is much larger too. It now includes OMIM disease links alongside Orphanet, and human orthologs from two prediction methods, OMA and InParanoid. Each ortholog is tagged with the method that supports it, so a call backed by both reads as higher confidence. Genes with a disease-linked human ortholog rose from about 525 to roughly 1,500. Finally, a new dictyBase Downloads page preserves dictyBase's bulk data files as local copies on this site. Gene information, mutant phenotypes, ontologies, protein data, GO annotations, and literature now download directly from us. Look for dictyBase Downloads in the top menu.
